topic: Antennas: dipoles, verticals, Yagis and special types (G9B, G9C, G9D; 35 pool questions)

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a random-wire HF antenna connected directly to the transmitter?

choices.A: It must be longer than 1 wavelength
choices.B: Station equipment may carry significant RF current
choices.C: It produces only vertically polarized radiation
choices.D: It is more effective on the lower HF bands than on the higher bands

questions.answer: Station equipment may carry significant RF current

questions.question: Which of the following is a common way to adjust the feed point impedance of an elevated quarter-wave ground-plane vertical antenna to be approximately 50 ohms?

choices.A: Slope the radials upward
choices.C: Lengthen the radials beyond one wavelength

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the radiation pattern of a quarter-wave ground-plane vertical antenna?

choices.A: Bi-directional in azimuth
choices.C: Hemispherical

questions.question: What is the radiation pattern of a dipole antenna in free space in a plane containing the conductor?

choices.A: It is a figure-eight at right angles to the antenna
choices.B: It is a figure-eight off both ends of the antenna
choices.C: It is a circle (equal radiation in all directions)
choices.D: It has a pair of lobes on one side of the antenna and a single lobe on the other side

questions.answer: It is a figure-eight at right angles to the antenna

questions.question: How does antenna height affect the azimuthal radiation pattern of a horizontal dipole HF antenna at elevation angles higher than about 45 degrees?

choices.A: If the antenna is too high, the pattern becomes unpredictable
choices.B: Antenna height has no effect on the pattern
choices.C: If the antenna is less than 1/2 wavelength high, the azimuthal pattern is almost omnidirectional
choices.D: If the antenna is less than 1/2 wavelength high, radiation off the ends of the wire is eliminated

questions.answer: If the antenna is less than 1/2 wavelength high, the azimuthal pattern is almost omnidirectional

questions.question: Where should the radial wires of a ground-mounted vertical antenna system be placed?

choices.A: As high as possible above the ground
choices.C: On the surface or buried a few inches below the ground
choices.D: At the center of the antenna

questions.answer: On the surface or buried a few inches below the ground

questions.question: How does the feed point impedance of a horizontal 1/2 wave dipole antenna change as the antenna height is reduced to 1/10 wavelength above ground?

choices.A: It steadily increases
choices.C: It peaks at about 1/8 wavelength above ground
choices.D: It is unaffected by the height above ground

questions.question: How does the feed point impedance of a 1/2 wave dipole change as the feed point is moved from the center toward the ends?

choices.A: It steadily increases
choices.C: It peaks at about 1/8 wavelength from the end
choices.D: It is unaffected by the location of the feed point

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of using a horizontally polarized as compared to a vertically polarized HF antenna?

choices.A: Lower ground losses
choices.C: Shorter radials

questions.question: What is the approximate length for a 1/2 wave dipole antenna cut for 14.250 MHz?

choices.A: 8 feet
choices.C: 24 feet

questions.question: What is the approximate length for a 1/2 wave dipole antenna cut for 3.550 MHz?

choices.A: 42 feet
choices.C: 132 feet

questions.question: What is the approximate length for a 1/4 wave monopole antenna cut for 28.5 MHz?

choices.A: 8 feet
choices.C: 16 feet

questions.question: Which of the following would increase the bandwidth of a Yagi antenna?

choices.A: Larger-diameter elements
choices.C: Loading coils in series with the element

questions.question: What is the approximate length of the driven element of a Yagi antenna?

choices.A: 1/4 wavelength
choices.C: 3/4 wavelength

questions.question: How do the lengths of a three-element Yagi reflector and director compare to that of the driven element?

choices.A: The reflector is longer, and the director is shorter
choices.B: The reflector is shorter, and the director is longer
choices.C: They are all the same length
choices.D: Relative length depends on the frequency of operation

questions.answer: The reflector is longer, and the director is shorter

questions.question: How does antenna gain in dBi compare to gain stated in dBd for the same antenna?

choices.A: Gain in dBi is 2.15 dB lower
choices.B: Gain in dBi is 2.15 dB higher
choices.C: Gain in dBd is 1.25 dBd lower
choices.D: Gain in dBd is 1.25 dBd higher

questions.answer: Gain in dBi is 2.15 dB higher

questions.question: What is the primary effect of increasing boom length and adding directors to a Yagi antenna?

choices.A: Gain increases
choices.C: Front-to-back ratio decreases

questions.question: What does “front-to-back ratio” mean in reference to a Yagi antenna?

choices.A: The number of directors versus the number of reflectors
choices.B: The relative position of the driven element with respect to the reflectors and directors
choices.C: The power radiated in the major lobe compared to that in the opposite direction
choices.D: The ratio of forward gain to dipole gain

questions.answer: The power radiated in the major lobe compared to that in the opposite direction

questions.question: What is meant by the “main lobe” of a directive antenna?

choices.A: The magnitude of the maximum vertical angle of radiation
choices.B: The point of maximum current in a radiating antenna element
choices.C: The maximum voltage standing wave point on a radiating element
choices.D: The direction of maximum radiated field strength from the antenna

questions.answer: The direction of maximum radiated field strength from the antenna

questions.question: In free space, how does the gain of two three-element, horizontally polarized Yagi antennas spaced vertically 1/2 wavelength apart typically compare to the gain of a single three-element Yagi?

choices.A: Approximately 1.5 dB higher
choices.C: Approximately 6 dB higher

questions.question: Which of the following can be adjusted to optimize forward gain, front-to-back ratio, or SWR bandwidth of a Yagi antenna?

choices.A: The physical length of the boom
choices.B: The number of elements on the boom
choices.C: The spacing of each element along the boom

questions.question: What is a beta or hairpin match?

choices.A: A shorted transmission line stub placed at the feed point of a Yagi antenna to provide impedance matching
choices.B: A 1/4 wavelength section of 75-ohm coax in series with the feed point of a Yagi to provide impedance matching
choices.C: A series capacitor selected to cancel the inductive reactance of a folded dipole antenna
choices.D: A section of 300-ohm twin-lead transmission line used to match a folded dipole antenna

questions.answer: A shorted transmission line stub placed at the feed point of a Yagi antenna to provide impedance matching

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of using a gamma match with a Yagi antenna?

choices.A: It does not require the driven element to be insulated from the boom
choices.B: It does not require any inductors or capacitors
choices.C: It is useful for matching multiband antennas

questions.answer: It does not require the driven element to be insulated from the boom

questions.question: Which of the following antenna types will be most effective as a near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS) antenna for short-skip communications on 40 meters during the day?

choices.A: A horizontal dipole placed between 1/10 and 1/4 wavelength above the ground
choices.B: A vertical antenna placed between 1/4 and 1/2 wavelength above the ground
choices.C: A horizontal dipole placed at approximately 1/2 wavelength above the ground
choices.D: A vertical dipole placed at approximately 1/2 wavelength above the ground

questions.answer: A horizontal dipole placed between 1/10 and 1/4 wavelength above the ground

questions.question: What is the feed point impedance of an end-fed half-wave antenna?

choices.A: Very low
choices.C: Approximately 300 ohms

questions.question: In which direction is the maximum radiation from a VHF/UHF “halo” antenna?

choices.A: Broadside to the plane of the halo
choices.C: Omnidirectional in the plane of the halo
choices.D: On the same side as the feed point

questions.answer: Omnidirectional in the plane of the halo

questions.question: What is the primary function of antenna traps?

choices.A: To enable multiband operation
choices.C: To provide balanced feed point impedance

questions.question: What is an advantage of vertically stacking horizontally polarized Yagi antennas?

choices.A: It allows quick selection of vertical or horizontal polarization
choices.B: It allows simultaneous vertical and horizontal polarization
choices.C: It narrows the main lobe in azimuth
choices.D: It narrows the main lobe in elevation

questions.answer: It narrows the main lobe in elevation

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of a log-periodic antenna?

choices.A: Wide bandwidth
choices.B: Higher gain per element than a Yagi antenna
choices.C: Harmonic suppression

questions.question: Which of the following describes a log-periodic antenna?

choices.A: Element length and spacing vary logarithmically along the boom
choices.B: Impedance varies periodically as a function of frequency
choices.C: Gain varies logarithmically as a function of frequency
choices.D: SWR varies periodically as a function of boom length

questions.answer: Element length and spacing vary logarithmically along the boom

questions.question: How does a “screwdriver” mobile antenna adjust its feed point impedance?

choices.A: By varying its body capacitance
choices.B: By varying the base loading inductance
choices.C: By extending and retracting the whip

questions.answer: By varying the base loading inductance

questions.question: What is the primary use of a Beverage antenna?

choices.A: Directional receiving for MF and low HF bands
choices.B: Directional transmitting for low HF bands
choices.C: Portable direction finding at higher HF frequencies
choices.D: Portable direction finding at lower HF frequencies

questions.answer: Directional receiving for MF and low HF bands

questions.question: In which direction or directions does an electrically small loop (less than 1/10 wavelength in circumference) have nulls in its radiation pattern?

choices.A: In the plane of the loop
choices.C: Broadside and in the plane of the loop

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of multiband antennas?

choices.A: They present low impedance on all design frequencies
choices.B: They must be used with an antenna tuner
choices.C: They must be fed with open wire line

questions.question: What is the common name of a dipole with a single central support?

choices.A: Inverted V
choices.C: Sloper
